findings.text: blocking: _trim keeps a pointer's value only when it is a scalar, so the `node` mapping every live pointer carries is dropped, _pointer_parts (reckon/crew/section_holds.py:57) then answers empty plan and section, _collect's target() returns None, and the batch's held-node check cannot see any live hold — reproduced against a real pointer in the crew home: untrimmed parts ('reasoning-text-in-tool-arguments', 'a-tool-call-carries-no-model-markup', 's6', 'investigate', 'complete'), trimmed parts ('', '', '', 'investigate', 'complete'), so a node another live run holds is queued again.

non-blocking: added() appends the untouched pointer, so the payload _trim removes from every pre-batch pointer returns once per entry the batch stores and the snapshot's retained bytes grow with the entry count, the growth this section exists to remove.

non-blocking: assert stored == LARGE compares the test's own argument with itself, because _peak_kib returns its `entries` parameter at line 144, so the assertion holds whatever queue_batch does and cannot catch a regression in what the batch stores.

non-blocking: `queued` is the batch's own subtraction (accepted - held_count, reckon/crew/dispatch_batch.py:1313) and no assertion reads the store, so §8's "each run's stored requests equal the base's" is unmeasured by this gate.

non-blocking: the per-node store read returns only rows whose indexed node column matches, so a delivered record written before node ids existed — which reckon/crew/section_holds.py:170 says must still hold its section — is absent whenever an entry names no node id, and that node is queued again.

non-blocking: _HeldOnce.rows re-implements the identity-and-filter step of held_node_rows at reckon/crew/section_holds.py:275 rather than sharing it, leaving two implementations of "the rows holding this plan's section node".

non-blocking: the cited after_suite log suite-head-final.log carries no `# revision:`, `# tree:` or `# command:` header and no `EXIT=` line, so the head arm's revision and exit status are unread from the run's own record, and the only log that does carry a revision header (suite-head.log) names bd1d5d0, not the reviewed head.
